title: GSPL Transmission Ltd - 544801 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: GSPL Transmission Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 8% YoY to INR 290 crore; EBITDA flat at INR 169 crore and company remains debt-free.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR 290 crore, up 8% YoY and 4.5% QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue was INR 567 crore, up 4.5%. EBITDA (excluding non-operating income) was about INR 169 crore against INR 168 crore a year earlier, with a 58.4% margin; PAT rose about 2% to INR 120 crore. Management reframed volume reporting from physical throughput to contractual volumes, and said it has about INR 3,500 crore of expansion capex (about 700 km, taking the Gujarat network to about 3,600 km) with about INR 300 crore spent in H1. The call was dominated by questions on the capex funding model, tariff review timing, PNGRB appeal, loss-making subsidiaries GIGL and GITL, and capital allocation versus buyback.

segments.name: High-pressure (HP) grid
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 9% YoY in Q2 FY27; management said HP network is at about 36 MMSCMD against the roughly 31.4-31.5 MMSCMD assumed in the last PNGRB tariff order.

segments.name: Low-pressure (LP) grid
segments.commentary: Volumes rose 30% YoY in Q2 FY27, the fastest-growing grid mentioned.

segments.name: HAPi grid
segments.commentary: Volumes rose 16% YoY in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: GIGL (JV)
segments.commentary: Operates about 1,439 km across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Punjab; combined GIGL and GITL capacity about 44-45 MMSCMD, with utilisation described as low double-digit and breakeven expected in about a couple of years.

segments.name: GITL (JV)
segments.commentary: Operates about 365 km connecting Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; management said it is profitable on a standalone basis, but it is loss-making at the group level per the analyst's framing, and major investment has been held back due to KG Basin sourcing issues.

guidance_outlook: About INR 3,500 crore expansion capex over 2 to 2.5 years; about INR 3,000 crore targeted by March 2028, with the balance spilling into April to June 2028.
Network to expand from about 2,900 km to about 3,600 km; capacity to rise from about 36.5 MMSCMD by about 8-9 MMSCMD.
Next tariff revision expected around 2028 (last revision April 2024); management will not speculate on tariff level and says the revision will not reduce tariffs.
Maintenance capex expected at INR 60-100 crore per year over the next couple of years.
Dividend payout expected to be maintained at current levels, subject to Board discretion; no guarantee on amount.
Interest income on deposits expected to fall toward zero as cash is deployed into capex, which will weigh on PAT.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex about INR 3,500 crore across more than 10 pipeline and connectivity projects totalling about 700 km; all projects board-approved and mostly in execution stage.
EPC contracts worth INR 1,800 crore awarded in July 2026 for Anjar-Palanpur pipeline, which is the major project stretching to March 2028; approvals said to be almost fully in place.

Other projects under implementation include Jamnagar-Dwarka, Vapi-Tarapur, Dahej-Bhadbhut and spur lines; Jamnagar-Dwarka linked to a Sun Petro-operated offshore Dwarka field with minimum 2.5 MMSCMD expected.
GIGL has a remaining capex of about INR 100-110 crore under execution and no major capex needs seen near term.
GITL: major investment deferred because of KG Basin sourcing issues; management says no PNGRB penalties incurred so far.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 12% YoY to 45 MMSCMD in Q2 FY27; management says volumes are now contractual rather than physical throughput, which is the basis for revenue.
Tariff regime: 12% post-tax RoCE on regulated assets; management said the 2024 revision was based on a 2023 filing; the next revision is expected in 2028.
Pending PNGRB appellate tribunal matter on prior claims; any favourable outcome would be credited prospectively via true-up, not retrospectively.
Revenue for GIGL and GITL is partly take-or-pay, which management said explains the gap between volume growth and revenue growth.
Other expenses rose in Q2 due to longer compressor operation to send more gas north; management says these are pass-through costs recoverable in the next tariff revision.

qa_highlights.question: Debt-to-equity plan for INR 3,500 crore expansion and whether board approval for debt is in place?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expansion will be funded mainly from internal accruals and cash, with limited financing if required; financing approvals are already in place and all projects are board-approved, with no further approvals needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume reporting change from physical to contractual, and how do tariffs reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier figures were physical volumes and the new figures are contractual, which align with revenue; some variation vs. tariff back-calculation is due to gross calorific value differences.

qa_highlights.question: Useful life of the 2,900 km network and next tariff revision timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial useful life is 30 years, extendable with recertification (PNGRB allows up to 10 years per tranche); next revision expected around 2028 and management does not expect tariffs to fall.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the PNGRB challenge and how true-up works?
qa_highlights.answer: The matter is still before the PNGRB appellate tribunal; any credit would be prospective only through subsequent transportation, and no prior claims have been adjudicated by PNGRB.

qa_highlights.question: How much of GIGL and GITL capacity is contracted and when will they break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are a few key customers but contracts are not yet enough for breakeven; it expects breakeven in about a couple of years and would revert with contract details later.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider a buyback or higher dividend, given cash and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is not top of the agenda and dividend is a Board decision; it intends to maintain the dividend at least at current rates but cannot guarantee amounts.

risks_watch: Anjar-Palanpur delivery by March 2028 is the critical path; the EPC contracts were awarded only in July 2026.
Land acquisition and right-of-way delays raised by an analyst; management said costs are capitalised and treated as pass-through, but no quantification given.
Subsidiary losses at GIGL and GITL: volumes remain well below capacity and breakeven is 'a couple of years' away; GITL capex deferred due to KG Basin sourcing issues.
PAT decline risk as cash is deployed and interest income on deposits falls toward zero.
Tariff outcome at the 2028 revision is not guided; the PNGRB appeal outcome is unknown and would be prospective only.
Capital allocation questions: investors pressed on buyback versus new pipeline investment at about 12% regulated return; management gave no buyback commitment.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, capex progress and the balance sheet, but evasive on tariff quantum, GIGL/GITL returns, buyback and dividend amounts, repeatedly deferring to the regulator or the Board.

adds.what: Expansion pipeline ~700 km (more than 10 pipeline and connectivity projects), network from ~2,900 km to ~3,600 km; capacity ~36.5 MMSCMD rising by ~8-9 MMSCMD

growth.why: Management guides ~INR 3,000 cr of the INR 3,500 cr expansion capex done by March 2028 (adding ~8-9 MMSCMD to ~36.5 MMSCMD), backed by INR 1,800 cr EPC contracts awarded July 2026 and board-approved projects, while H1 FY27 revenue grew only 4.5% and EBITDA was flat.
